source_name: Security Considerations for ML-DSA
requirement: Zeroize signing keys when no longer needed to prevent later compromise.
evidence_quote: Zeroizing the signing key when the signer has no further need of it prevents later compromise.

source_name: Security Considerations for ML-DSA
requirement: Securely delete cached expanded signing key material when no longer needed.
evidence_quote: This cached expanded key material requires the same protections as the seed signing key and benefits from being securely deleted when no longer needed.

source_name: Security Considerations for ML-DSA
requirement: Assess side-channel attack possibilities and use implementations resistant to such leakage.
evidence_quote: The implementor will need to assess this possibility and possibly use an implementation that is resistant to such leakage.

source_name: Security Considerations for ML-DSA
requirement: Use hedged signing mode to mitigate fault injection and side-channel attacks.
evidence_quote: hedged signing is the safer default in all environments, and is essential where fault injection or side-channel attacks are a concern.

source_name: Security Considerations for ML-DSA
requirement: Use available randomness sources for signing rather than falling back to deterministic signing on constrained platforms.
evidence_quote: Implementations on constrained platforms that lack access to a full-strength RBG should still use whatever randomness source is available for rnd rather than falling back to deterministic signing.

source_name: Security Considerations for ML-DSA
requirement: Define a fixed context string for a given protocol's use case to prevent cross-protocol attacks.
evidence_quote: Defining a fixed context string for a given protocol's use case prevents cross-protocol attacks.

source_name: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023
requirement: Publish a point of contact for security issue reporting and specify timelines for acknowledgment and status updates.
evidence_quote: The following information must be published— (a) at least one point of contact to allow a person (“P”) to report to the manufacturer security issues... and (b) when P will receive— (i) an acknowledgment of the receipt of a security issues report; and (ii) status updates until the resolution of the reported security issues.

source_name: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023
requirement: Publish the defined support period for security updates, ensuring it is accessible, clear, and free of charge.
evidence_quote: The defined support period must be published. ... The information in sub-paragraphs (2) and (3) must be accessible, clear and transparent, and must be made available to a person (“P”)— (a) without prior request for such information being made; (b) in English; (c) free of charge

source_name: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023
requirement: Retain a copy of the statement of compliance for the longer of 10 years or the defined support period.
evidence_quote: the manufacturer of the product must retain a copy of the statement of compliance relating to the product for whichever is the longer of— (a) a period of 10 years beginning with the date on which the statement of compliance was issued, and (b) the defined support period for the product set out in the statement of compliance.

source_name: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023
requirement: Ensure passwords are unique per product or user-defined, and not derived from incremental counters or public identifiers without encryption.
evidence_quote: Passwords must be— (a) unique per product; or (b) defined by the user of the product. source_name: The Product Security and Telecommunications Infrastructure (Security Requirements for Relevant Connectable Products) Regulations 2023

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Authorization servers MUST include RS256 among their supported signature algorithms for JWT access tokens.
evidence_quote: Authorization servers and resource servers conforming to this specification MUST include RS256 (as defined in [ RFC7518 ] ) among their supported signature algorithms.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Authorization servers SHOULD use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata to advertise signing keys via jwks_uri and issuer values.
evidence_quote: Authorization servers SHOULD use OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata [ RFC8414 ] to advertise to resource servers their signing keys via "jwks_uri" and what "iss" claim value to expect via the "issuer" metadata value.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST validate the signature of all incoming JWT access tokens using the algorithm specified in the JWT alg Header Parameter.
evidence_quote: The resource server MUST validate the signature of all incoming JWT access tokens according to [ RFC7515 ] using the algorithm specified in the JWT "alg" Header Parameter.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST reject any JWT in which the value of alg is none.
evidence_quote: The resource server MUST reject any JWT in which the value of "alg" is "none".

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST verify that the typ header value is at+jwt or application/at+jwt and reject tokens carrying any other value.
evidence_quote: The resource server MUST verify that the "typ" header value is "at+jwt" or "application/at+jwt" and reject tokens carrying any other value.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST validate that the aud claim contains a resource indicator value corresponding to an identifier the resource server expects for itself.
evidence_quote: The resource server MUST validate that the "aud" claim contains a resource indicator value corresponding to an identifier the resource server expects for itself. The JWT access token MUST be rejected if "aud" does not contain a resource indicator of the current resource server as a valid audience.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST ensure the current time is before the time represented by the exp claim.
evidence_quote: The current time MUST be before the time represented by the "exp" claim.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST use the keys provided by the authorization server for signature validation.
evidence_quote: The resource server MUST use the keys provided by the authorization server.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Resource servers MUST handle validation errors by including the error code invalid_token in the response.
evidence_quote: In particular, in case of any failure in the validation checks listed above, the authorization server response MUST include the error code "invalid_token".

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Authorization servers MUST NOT issue a JWT access token if the authorization granted by the token would be ambiguous.
evidence_quote: The authorization server MUST NOT issue a JWT access token if the authorization granted by the token would be ambiguous.

source_name: JSON Web Token (JWT) Profile for OAuth 2.0 Access Tokens
requirement: Authorization servers MUST use a distinct identifier as an aud claim value to uniquely identify access tokens issued for distinct resources.
evidence_quote: To prevent cross-JWT confusion, authorization servers MUST use a distinct identifier as an "aud" claim value to uniquely identify access tokens issued by the same issuer for distinct resources.

source_name: Fully-Specified Algorithms for JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE)
requirement: Utilize fully-specified algorithm identifiers in new deployments in preference to deprecated polymorphic identifiers, unless documented operational or regulatory requirements prevent migration.
evidence_quote: There is a preferred mechanism to achieve functionality similar to that referenced by the identifier; this replacement functionality SHOULD be utilized in new deployments in preference to the deprecated identifier, unless there exist documented operational or regulatory requirements that prevent migration away from the deprecated identifier.

source_name: Fully-Specified Algorithms for JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE)
requirement: Prohibit the use of algorithm identifiers designated as 'Prohibited' and the functionality they reference.
evidence_quote: The identifier and the functionality that it references MUST NOT be used. (Identifiers may be designated as "Prohibited" due to security flaws, for instance.)

source_name: Fully-Specified Algorithms for JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE)
requirement: Ensure that the 'alg' value in JOSE encryption specifies all parameters for key establishment or derives them from the 'enc' value, and that the 'enc' value specifies all parameters for symmetric encryption.
evidence_quote: To perform fully-specified encryption in JOSE, the "alg" value MUST specify all parameters for key establishment or derive some of them from the accompanying "enc" value, and the "enc" value MUST specify all parameters for symmetric encryption.

source_name: Fully-Specified Algorithms for JSON Object Signing and Encryption (JOSE) and CBOR Object Signing and Encryption (COSE)
requirement: Ensure that the outer 'alg' value in COSE encryption specifies all parameters for key establishment, and the inner 'alg' value specifies all parameters for symmetric encryption.
evidence_quote: To perform fully-specified encryption in COSE, the outer "alg" value MUST specify all parameters for key establishment, and the inner "alg" value MUST specify all parameters for symmetric encryption.
